name: Cudrania tricuspidata extract
short: Few data: one 8-week trial (100 adults, 83 analysed): adverse events did not differ from placebo (p = 0.523); no counts or types given. Lab studies: extracts inhibit drug-metabolising enzymes.
text: This entry covers Cudrania tricuspidata extract taken by mouth as tablets. The only human safety data found come from one trial: in an 8-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicentre study, 100 adults with any condition in the Rome IV criteria (the title says functional dyspepsia) took a Cudrania tricuspidata extract tablet or a maltodextrin placebo, 83 were analysed, and adverse events did not differ between groups (p = 0.523); the abstract does not give the number or type of events. No case reports of harm were found. Interactions (laboratory data only): in laboratory enzyme assays, leaf extracts strongly inhibited the drug-metabolising enzymes CYP1A2 and CYP2C8, and in human liver microsomes a compound isolated from the root (cudratricusxanthone A) reversibly inhibited CYP1A2, CYP2C8 and CYP2C9; these are laboratory findings, and no study in people was found. The cited sources give no data on pregnancy or children.
